explanation: Their other name, kettledrums, comes from their large copper or fibreglass bowls. Moving the pedal tightens or slackens the drumhead, raising or lowering the note.

claims.text: Modern timpani are tuned to definite pitches, usually with a foot pedal.
Snare drums, bongos and djembes are not tuned with a foot pedal.
Timpani are also called kettledrums, after the shape of their large copper or fibreglass bowls.
A timpani pedal changes the tension of the drumhead, raising or lowering the pitch.
